title: SSC CHSL English
summary: SSC CHSL Tier I English past questions from 24 shifts, 2024 to 2025, five a day. Questions SSC asked again and the question types it keeps asking come first, ranked together by how often they were asked, then every other question. A set of linked items counts as one question.
note: Repeats are counted across the 24 SSC CHSL Tier I shifts, July 2024 and November 2025, including questions SSC reprinted word for word. SSC writes fresh questions for almost every shift; a word it asks again is a repeat, and a grammar rule it keeps testing is a type. Vocabulary, idioms, cloze and comprehension passages are each their own fact, so they are not grouped into types. Groups were found by a chapter-by-chapter reading (scripts/homework/REVIEW_BRIEF_SSC.md) and checked in the main session. Questions marked defective are left out.

groups.label: Impersonal passive (It was said / believed that ...) into active with People or They
Imperative and passive with 'Let ... be' (Let it be made sure, Leave no stone unturned)
Question sentence into passive (Did/Will/Who ... ? to Was/Will ... be ...?)
Future perfect voice change: will have + V3 and will have been + V3
Perfect tense voice change: has/have/had + V3 and has/had been + V3
Simple past voice change: V2 and was/were + V3
Continuous tense voice change: is/was + -ing and is/was being + V3
Modal or semi-modal voice change (must, could, has to, is to, is supposed to + be + V3)
Passage set: voice or sentence-form change of a passage sentence plus word meanings and one fact question
Direct to indirect speech: a statement with tense back-shift and pronoun change
Direct to indirect speech: a wh-question (asked what/why/who + statement order)
Reported yes/no question (asked if ...) into direct speech
Reported statement into direct speech: undo the back-shift (had to have, that day to today)
Exclamatory sentence in narration (exclaimed that / What a ...!)
Dependent preposition after a verb or adjective (accounted for, insisted on, accused of)
Contrast connector in the blank (even though, nevertheless)
Passage set mixing grammar items (voice, phrase function, tense, idiom) with word meanings and one main-idea question
Passage set of fact, inference and main-idea questions with one word meaning
Four steps of one person's process: put them in time order
'a' before a vowel sound should be 'an' (a umbrella, a oasis)
Missing or wrong 'the' (the Earth, the injured, the most, most of the tea)
Subject-verb agreement: singular or plural subject with the wrong verb form
Verb agrees with the head noun, not the noun after 'of' or 'along with'
Pronoun agreeing with 'each of' or 'one' (her, one's)
Apostrophe in possessives (its not it's, company's)
Future continuous form: will/shall be + -ing (not will being)
If/when clause takes the present, main clause takes will
'No sooner ... than' (not when or that)
Sequence of tenses: past main clause takes a past time clause
Verb pattern: gerund, infinitive or that-clause after a verb (like playing, deny attending, prevent from)
Adjective vs adverb (fast not fastly, hard not hardly, behave violently, speak well)
Parallel structure: items joined by 'and' in the same form
Fixed preposition after a word (obliged to, agree with, married to, made of)
Preposition of place or movement (over the city, up the valley, out of the car, beside the lake)
Preposition of time (throughout, after a long time, before bed)
Antonym of 'important': trivial
Homophones born and borne in a sentence
Spelling of 'privilege'
